sections.h2: How to sell a house in Lebanon
sections.html:
A Lebanon owner can realistically take one of three routes: engage an agent, locate a buyer personally, or hand the house to a cash buyer as it is. Think about the house's condition, your deadline and how much price you would give up for speed.

Growth here has been rapid. Lebanon counted 53,412 people in mid-2025, 38.8% above the April 2020 base of 38,495. Of all housing units, 62.4% are owner-occupied, with a 2020-2024 median value of $378,400, and the median renter pays $1,306.

  • Listing: the biggest pool of buyers, with timing set by their inspection and loan.
  • Private sale: no agent fee, but the paperwork is yours.
  • Cash purchase: no showings or repairs, and you name the closing date.

The Wilson County seat, Lebanon, lies about 25 miles east of downtown Nashville, and commuters drive demand. Interstate 40 passes south of the city with three Lebanon exits, U.S. 70 heads west to Nashville, and the WeGo Star commuter train ends here with weekday service. A partial beltway is formed by Hartmann Drive and Maddox-Simpson Parkway. The usual commute is 27.0 minutes, and median household income for 2020-2024 is $72,848.

In a listing, lead with how far the house is from the interstate, the train station and the schools. Commuting buyers weigh those before finishes, and a clear answer heads off questions.

Most of the city sits in Lebanon Special School District, which teaches pre-kindergarten through eighth grade. Its roughly 4,600 students attend five elementary schools (Byars Dowdy, Castle Heights, Coles Ferry, Jones Brummett and Sam Houston) and two middle schools, Walter J. Baird and Winfree Bryant.

For high school, students go to Wilson County Schools, which also serves a few small corners of Lebanon at every grade. Because district lines decide a buyer's school, point buyers to the district for confirmation rather than a listing description. LSSD has an address search tool on its own site.

sections.h2: City and Wilson County property taxes
sections.html:
A Lebanon house is taxed twice, once by the city and once by Wilson County, at different payment points. City tax of $0.4054 per $100 of assessed value is paid at the city property tax office, 200 N. Castle Heights Avenue.

Lebanon and Wilson County tax calendar
DateEvent
January 1Value of all property is set as of this date
May 20Assessor posts values to the roll and tells owners about any change
June 1County Board of Equalization opens its appeal hearings
August 1Last day to file with the state, or 45 days after the county board rules if that is later
October 1 to February 28City tax can be paid with no penalty
March 1City adds a 1.5% monthly penalty

The assessor supplies values and the state prints city notices, which makes 615-444-8661 the number for address fixes. Mid-October is when county bills go out; the Wilson County Trustee, at 228 E. Main Street, Room 102, takes payment until the end of February.

Begin at the Wilson County Property Assessor's office, in person or by phone, because clerical mistakes explain many disputes. Beyond that is the Wilson County Board of Equalization, five property owners: one seat from Lebanon, one from Mt. Juliet and three from the county.

The board opens June 1 and sits until that year's work is done; the assessor runs a newspaper notice about ten days before. Book a hearing slot by phone or at the counter in late May or early June. You can attend yourself, send a relative or attorney, and bring witnesses. A lower assessment carries to the next owner, so if the number looks wrong, appeal before listing.

sections.h2: Permits, short-term rentals and building rules
sections.html:
Two departments share the load. Zoning enforcement officials deal with pools, fences, sidewalks and short-term rental permits, and they staff the Board of Zoning Appeals, which rules on setback and accessory structure variances. The same staff support the Historic Zoning Commission and its certificates of appropriateness.

  • The Chief Building Official's staff, who hold ICC and state certifications, issue building permits and run inspections.
  • Electrical inspections are not done by the city. State of Tennessee deputy electrical inspectors do them.
  • New single-family and townhome projects follow a five-step residential development process before a certificate of occupancy is issued.

If guests ever stayed short-term in the house, call the zoning office at 615-444-3647 and ask which permit is on file.

sections.h2: Recording the deed and tax relief
sections.html:
Deeds for Lebanon houses go to the Wilson County Register of Deeds. Transfer tax charged by the state is 37 cents per $100 of price.

Older or disabled owners may qualify for state and county tax relief, and seniors may be eligible for a tax freeze on a primary residence. Both come through the Wilson County Trustee at 615-444-0894 (option 2). Ask what a mid-year sale does to either program.

sections.h2: Selling with a tenant in the house
sections.html: A house with tenants can still be sold. Show buyers the lease early and ask the title company how it changes closing. Someone buying as is can take on a rented property, and the contract can settle what happens to the tenant. Before listing, look at the roof, gutters, grading and cooling equipment, because inspectors raise those first and cash buyers price them in.

A ready paper trail speeds up a Lebanon sale. Gather the latest city tax bill and county tax bill, the assessor's value notice if you kept it, and a payoff letter from your lender. Rented to short-term guests at some point? Add the permit details from the zoning office. The title company and a buyer's lender will want most of this, and one folder can save days.

Decide too whether to contest your assessment before you list. The calendar above gives the windows: a talk with the assessor first, the county board from June 1, and the state deadline of August 1, unless 45 days after the county's ruling comes later.

sections.h2: What a cash sale skips in Lebanon
sections.html: When the buyer has a mortgage, the sale waits for an appraisal and loan approval, and an inspection can reopen the price. A cash buyer sets all of that aside. The remaining steps are identical: title work, splitting the year's taxes between buyer and seller, and filing the deed with the Wilson County Register of Deeds. Request a written closing date, and with a rented house ask how the lease will be handled at the table. Then confirm that the title company will pay both the city and county bills from the proceeds.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Lebanon house that has tenants?
faqs.a: Yes. Give the buyer the lease early and ask the title company how it affects closing. A buyer taking the house as is can accept a tenant, and the contract can cover the tenant's plans.

faqs.q: When are Lebanon city property taxes due?
faqs.a: You can pay city taxes from October 1 through February 28. Starting March 1, a penalty of 1.5% a month is added.

faqs.q: Who decides what my Lebanon house is worth for taxes?
faqs.a: The Wilson County Property Assessor sets the value, and the city applies its own rate to it. Disputes go to the assessor first and the Board of Equalization second.

faqs.q: Is there a tax freeze for older Lebanon homeowners?
faqs.a: Yes. The Wilson County Trustee runs a freeze that holds a senior's tax amount steady on a primary residence, along with a relief program for older, disabled and disabled veteran owners. Call 615-444-0894 and pick option 2.

faqs.q: Does the city inspect electrical work on a Lebanon house?
faqs.a: No. State of Tennessee deputy inspectors do electrical inspections, not the Lebanon Building Inspection Department.
